a1
At first, the whole earth spoke one language.
b1
Moving east, they settled on a plain in Shinar, and said: let's make bricks and bake them hard.
c1
Then: let's build a city and a tower with its top in the heavens.
c2
And let's make a name for ourselves, so we won't be scattered.
c3
But the Lord came down to see the city and the tower.
c4
He saw one people with one language, and said: let us confuse their speech.
d1
Suddenly, they could no longer understand one another.
d2
The Lord scattered them over all the earth, and the building stopped.
d3
That is why the place was called Babel.
e1
Genesis then follows Shem's family down to a man named Terah.
e2
Terah's son Abram had a wife named Sarai, who had no child.
e3
Terah led them out of Ur toward Canaan, but they settled in Haran.
h1
At Babel, people built to make a name for themselves.
h2
In the very next chapter, God tells Abram: I will make your name great.
h3
Pride builds towers to be seen. Trust lets God do the building.
h4
Today, build something for God, not just for your name.
i
What are you building to make a name for yourself?
